theme: Who shall sojourn on your holy hill?
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 15. This short psalm asks who may dwell with God and gives the answer in a list of ten character marks. Read it slowly, and notice that the list is about everyday integrity.
settingTheScene: Psalm 15 is a psalm of David, probably used as an entrance liturgy when worshipers approached the sanctuary. A question is asked: who may be a guest in God’s tent? The answer is a description of a person whose life matches their worship. James would call this a doer of the word. The psalm raises a question that only the gospel can answer: who is so blameless?
observation: “O LORD, who shall sojourn in your tent? Who shall dwell on your holy hill?” (v. 1).
“He who walks blamelessly and does what is right” (v. 2).
“Who does not slander with his tongue and does no evil to his friend” (v. 3).
“In whose eyes a vile person is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD” (v. 4).
“Who swears to his own hurt and does not change” (v. 4).
“Who does not put out his money at interest” (v. 5).
“He who does these things shall never be moved” (v. 5).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a question about access: “O LORD, who shall sojourn in your tent? Who shall dwell on your holy hill?” To sojourn means to stay as a guest, and the tent is the sanctuary where God meets his people. The question is not about earning a place but about the kind of person who belongs there. In the Old Testament, to be close to God’s holy presence is a great privilege and requires holiness.

The answer has three layers. First, general character: “He who walks blamelessly and does what is right and speaks truth in his heart.” Blamelessness means integrity, a life that is whole. Truth is spoken not only with the lips but in the heart; no gap exists between inner conviction and outer speech. Second, how he treats his neighbor: he “does not slander with his tongue and does no evil to his friend, nor takes up a reproach against his friend.” Gossip and slander are named along with outright harm. Third, how he deals with the world: he despises a vile person (does not admire the corrupt) and honors those who fear the LORD. He keeps his promise even when it costs him: “who swears to his own hurt and does not change.” His word is his bond. He does not exploit the needy by charging them interest (Exodus 22:25) and does not take bribes against the innocent.

“He who does these things shall never be moved.” This is the life the whole of Scripture calls for. But who can say that he fits this description? None of us. Here we see our need for Christ. He is the one who walked blamelessly, who spoke truth from the heart, who kept his word even to his own hurt, going to the cross. He alone ascended the hill of the LORD with clean hands. Those who are in him are welcomed into God’s presence, not because they match this psalm but because he does, and his righteousness is counted as theirs. And then, by the Spirit, he begins to form this character in us. The list in Psalm 15 is both a mirror and a goal.
connection: Psalm 24:3-6 asks a similar question. Isaiah 33:14-16 and Micah 6:6-8 also describe who may dwell with God. Exodus 22:25 and Deuteronomy 23:19-20 forbid interest on loans to the poor. Exodus 23:8 forbids bribes. Matthew 5:33-37 teaches on oaths. Ephesians 4:25-32 tells believers to put away falsehood and slander. 1 Peter 2:22 says no deceit was found in Christ’s mouth. Hebrews 4:14-16 invites us to draw near through our high priest. 2 Corinthians 5:21 says we become the righteousness of God in him. James 1:26-27 and 3:1-12 also test religion by speech and conduct.
application:
Read the ten marks slowly and mark the two where you most need growth. Ask the Spirit for help.

Ask whether you have broken a promise that cost you. If you can still keep it, do so.

Thank Christ that you are welcomed into God’s tent because of his righteousness.
prayerPrompts: Ask who may dwell on God’s hill, and tell him you cannot by your own righteousness.
Thank Jesus for walking blamelessly and speaking truth.
Ask him to make you truthful and faithful.
